subject: Urgent: p99 regressions impacting BrightMart checkout — apparent client retries

Subject: Severe latency spike during checkout (p99 up 6x)

Hi Kimberly —

We started seeing a large spike in checkout latency around 08:45 UTC this morning. p95 is up ~3x and p99 is ~6x compared to our baseline; customers are reporting failed checkout attempts. Our engineers captured request traces and a sample request sequence (attached: brightmart-request-log.txt).

Key notes from our side:
- Impact window: ~08:45–09:10 UTC
- Error symptoms: timeouts on our side, some 5xx responses observed by our logs
- This is affecting ~12% of checkout traffic at peak and causing cart abandonment

Can Redwood confirm whether this was a hosted API incident? We need an urgent RCA and plan — BrightMart is taking this to the incident ops table now.

Please escalate.

Thanks,
Julia Ramos

Hi Julia —

Quick update after looking at host-side telemetry and the request samples you provided. Attached is a dashboard snapshot (redwood-p99-spike-dashboard.png) showing the p95/p99 jump at ~08:45 UTC. A few preliminary observations:

- Server processing times (time in runtime) do increase slightly for the affected window but not enough to fully explain the magnitude of the p99 jump. Typical server-side tail is ~120ms; spikes show blocks around 250–600ms for a subset of requests.
- Looking at ingress logs and client IPs, we see a pattern where the same request_id (or identical payloads) are arriving repeatedly from the same client IPs in very short succession — often within 1–3s of each other.
- Correlated traces suggest many of those subsequent requests completed successfully on the server (200) but your logs mark them as failures because the client had already retried. In other words, there appear to be client-side timeouts + immediate retries amplifying traffic.

I've attached a small sample of the repeated-request series (excerpted). Can your engineering team confirm whether their SDK is configured to retry aggressively on timeouts or network errors? Also please provide the SDK version; we have seen behavioral differences across versions.

Cc-ing Sean to validate if any edge-network transient could have caused early client-side timeouts.

Thanks,

Monica —

Thanks for the quick look. Our infra team ran a short check and says we do not have an intentionally aggressive retry policy; we use Redwood's official SDK v2.4.1 with default settings. I'm attaching a signed log extract from our side that shows our client timeout firing at ~2.5s followed by an immediate retry by the SDK.

We are concerned because from our perspective the initial request appears to have hit Redwood and completed (we received a 200 on the retry path) but our user sees a timeout. This looks like the API returned, but the client timed out first. Can you confirm whether network-level retransmits or NAT gateway delays could cause the SDK to decide the request timed out even though the backend completed? We need a definitive root cause — our ops and CTO are involved.

Julia Ramos
Head of Platform, BrightMart

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ramos <julia@brightmart.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-17T11:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Preliminary triage: p99 spike (BrightMart)

Hi all —

I dug into the network and runtime traces. Findings below (summary first, details after):

Summary:
- Host runtime processed the original requests in timeframes that should not have triggered the client's 2.5s timeout in normal conditions. Many of the server-side logs show 200 responses within 400–800ms.
- We observed TCP-level connection resets and SYN retransmits between BrightMart client subnets and our edge POPs during the spike window. Those retransmits can cause the client to not receive the ACK/response before its local timeout fires, prompting an SDK retry.
- Additionally, SDK v2.4.1 has a known behavior (reported in our issue tracker) where certain network errors are treated as retryable and retried immediately with no exponential backoff. See https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1287 for the root discussion.

What this means for the incident:
- The perceived API latency p99 is inflated at BrightMart's side because timeouts + immediate client retries are creating duplicate traffic and surfacing the earlier local timeout to end-users. In other words, the backend frequently returned in time, but the client had already given up and retried.

Recommendations / actions:
1) BrightMart: upgrade SDK to v2.5.0 which contains the retry/backoff fix. Apply a conservative client timeout (e.g., 5s) so transient network retransmits don't trigger early retries.
2) Redwood: we will add a per-customer heuristic to detect high-rate duplicate payloads from the same IP and apply short-term server-side de-duplication/throttling to prevent amplification while we work on longer-term controls.
3) Joint RCA: exchange packet captures and NAT gateway logs to isolate the network layer; I suggest a joint call with your network team.

I've attached an exported trace archive in S3 (s3-signed-log-archive.zip) with anonymized connection-level events and a sample of the duplicate request sequences showing server 200s following the client timeout.

If helpful, we can schedule a 1-hour postmortem this week with our SREs and your network engineers.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Incident summary and remediation plan (BrightMart p99 spike)

Julia / BrightMart execs —

First, sincere apologies for the customer impact this week. We appreciate BrightMart's prompt collaboration. Below is a succinct summary, immediate remediation, and next steps.

Incident summary:
- Symptom: sharp p95/p99 regressions observed by BrightMart at ~08:45 UTC 2026-01-15, causing user-facing timeouts and failed checkouts.
- Root cause (joint): transient network-level retransmits between BrightMart subnets and our edge POPs caused some client requests to not observe server ACKs in time. The BrightMart SDK (v2.4.1) then retried immediately on those local timeouts. Those retries amplified load and made BrightMart-observed tail latency appear worse than server-side processing would indicate.

Immediate remediation we will execute this week:
- Redwood: deploy a customer-scoped duplicate-request detection heuristic (temporary throttle) to mitigate retry amplification within 24h.
- BrightMart: upgrade to SDK v2.5.0 (contains improved backoff and fewer immediate retries). We will provide a short compatibility test and assistance.
- Joint: schedule a network-level packet capture session to identify whether NAT gateway or ISP path contributed to retransmits; shared action owner: BrightMart network team + Redwood SREs (Sean).

Compensation and follow-up:
- Redwood will apply a one-month credit against hosted API usage for the impacted period (details to follow via Kimberly).
- We propose a 60-minute postmortem next week to finalize the RCA and confirm mitigations.

Action items (owners):
- BrightMart: upgrade SDK + run compatibility tests (Julia / BrightMart Eng)
- Redwood: deploy server-side duplicate suppression + prepare postmortem deck (Sean / Monica)
- Kimberly: coordinate credits and exec updates (Kimberly)

If you agree, Kimberly will follow up with a proposed time for the postmortem and the credit paperwork. We want to make sure this does not recur.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
